# A Model field is spelled the way the platform declared it. Platforms declare
# them verbatim -- a node id, a slot, a canvas context -- which is what
# codegen.ModelFieldRef means by `m.<name>`.
#
# The Go renderer exported them instead, and did it on some paths and not
# others, so one field became two names:
#
#     inc  *widget.Button        // declared
#     m.Inc = widget.NewButton() // written, through MutTargetField
#     m.inc.SetText("+")         // read, through evalIdent
#
# ExportName is the identity on the synthesized ids (`__n1`), which is why this
# went unseen: it takes a node id a program actually wrote to break, and then
# no fyne or gtk4 program with a tagged widget compiled at all -- an ordinary
# `generate`, not just a test build.
#
# `sngl test` is the assertion because it compiles what it generates. The
# fixture deliberately does not click: driving an event is a separate gap.

sngl test --platform none tagged.sngl
stdout 'ok'
sngl test --platform html tagged.sngl
stdout 'ok'
sngl test --platform bubbletea tagged.sngl
stdout 'ok'
sngl test --platform fyne tagged.sngl
stdout 'ok'
sngl test --platform gtk4 tagged.sngl
stdout 'ok'

# The same, as an ordinary build: the emitted field and every reference to it
# agree on one name.
sngl generate --platform=fyne --lang=go --out=fy tagged.sngl
grep 'inc  *\*widget.Button' fy/model.go
grep 'm\.inc = widget\.NewButton' fy/model.go
grep 'm\.inc\.OnTapped = m\.inc_click_handler' fy/model.go
! grep 'm\.Inc' fy/model.go

-- tagged.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"
import . "sngl:test"
import app "sngl:app"

component counter ui {
    var n = 3
    vbox {
        text(value="{n}")
        button #inc(text="+", @click { n = n + 1 })
    }
}

func testInitial(t Test, c counter) {
    t.assert(c.n == 3)
}

app.window {
}
